answer: Each identity must lease one numbered drying rack in a regional walnut-hulling hall, issued only up to the hall's licensed floor capacity. Enrollment photographs the rack plate, ties a uniquely dyed thread through its seal hole, and binds that seal to one signing key. Inspectors later demand a time-stamped photo of the intact thread; peers reject a second key on the same rack or a broken seal and slash the lease bond. Because racks cannot be subdivided, every fake ID needs its own lease and seal, so attacker cost stays linear and rises at the nadir of vacant racks.
